name: Low
label: Sub Pop
lede: A married couple from Duluth, members of the LDS Church, started Low in 1993 and played as slowly and softly as they could while grunge was loud. They kept at it for almost thirty years, until Mimi Parker's death in November 2022 ended the band.

eras.title: Quiet in the grunge years
eras.text: Alan Sparhawk and Parker had known each other since grade school in Clearbrook, Minnesota. In Duluth they started a band as a half-joke experiment: how would a crowd take music this slow and this soft when everyone else was playing loud?

years.h: Sparhawk and Parker play Low's first two shows at the RecyclaBell
years.p: Alan Sparhawk and Mimi Parker, both members of the LDS Church, recruit bassist John Nichols. Parker plays one snare, one cymbal and one floor tom, almost always with brushes.
years.xp:
Before Low, Sparhawk played in Zen Identity across the bridge in Superior, Wisconsin. He and Nichols started with improvised quiet themes. Sparhawk has described the idea as half joke, half experiment: what would Duluth crowds do with music this quiet while grunge was the loudest thing going?

The band never liked the word slowcore.

years.h: A Virgin imprint puts out Low's debut, I Could Live in Hope
years.p: [[Kramer|d898e082-70d1-4a86-ac8e-ecdf89892994]] produces it for Vernon Yard, and John Nichols plays bass on what is his only album with Low.

years.h: Zak Sally takes over on bass for Long Division
years.p: Sally replaces John Nichols for the second album, again produced by [[Kramer|d898e082-70d1-4a86-ac8e-ecdf89892994]], and stays ten years.

years.h: College radio plays "Over the Ocean" from The Curtain Hits the Cast
years.p: [[Kramer|d898e082-70d1-4a86-ac8e-ecdf89892994]] produces again, and the band becomes a critics' favorite.

eras.title: Albini, then a snowball fight on TV
eras.text: On Kranky, Low made two records with Steve Albini that many fans still rank among their best, then a third mixed at Peter Gabriel's studio. A hymn-slow Christmas cover ended up in a Gap ad.

years.h: Nine days with Steve Albini in Chicago
years.p: Low records Secret Name at [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]]'s Electrical Audio, its first album for Kranky. Zak Sally adds Optigan to some songs.

years.h: Secret Name arrives on Kranky
years.p: Tugboat releases it in the UK. The Washington Post said Low had done something new without losing its serenity.

years.cap: Alan Sparhawk and Mimi Parker, Duluth
years.src: Wikipedia: Things We Lost in the Fire
years.h: A second record with Albini, Things We Lost in the Fire
years.p: Opening with "Sunflower" and closing with the instrumental "In Metal," it scores 87 on Metacritic. The Guardian's 2019 critics' poll ranks it 93rd of the century so far.
years.xp:
Pitchfork put it at 117 on its list of the best albums of the 2000s. Low played the whole record at a Don't Look Back show in 2006.

Argentine writer Mariana Enriquez, a fan, named her story collection after it.

years.h: Trust is mixed at Peter Gabriel's Real World
years.p: Tom Herbers and Eric Swanson record it and Tchad Blake mixes it at Real World Studios. It's the last Low album on Kranky.

years.h: A slow-motion Gap snowball fight runs on Low's "Little Drummer Boy"
years.p: Gap uses the band's hymn-slow cover of the Christmas song. A remix of Low's "Halflight" turns up in The Mothman Prophecies.

years.h: Zak Sally quits Low, then says he's staying
years.p: The band posts that everyone has had to work through some personal things, and that the good news is Sally is remaining.
years.xp: He does stay, for a while. He leaves for good in October 2005 after ten years.

years.h: Low opens for Radiohead across Europe
years.p: [[Radiohead|a74b1b7f-71a5-4011-9441-d0b5e4122711]] take Low on a European tour in July, with Sally back on bass.

eras.title: Louder, on Sub Pop
eras.text: Low signed to Sub Pop, made a louder record and charted in the US. Then Sparhawk cancelled a tour and told fans about his depression.

years.h: Low leaves Kranky for Sub Pop
years.p: Low joins Sub Pop. Its own Chairkickers' Union label puts out A Lifetime of Temporary Relief: 10 Years of B-Sides and Rarities.

years.h: Dave Fridmann produces The Great Destroyer
years.p: The Village Voice heard comparatively thunderous verve. It's Low's first album to chart in the US.

years.h: Sparhawk cancels the tour and tells fans about his depression
years.p: He calls off the second leg of The Great Destroyer tour and publishes a statement about his struggle with depression. In August he's back on the road with [[Mark Kozelek|99f4b23d-3711-4efe-ad71-9572158e234c]].

years.h: A Navy chaplain's pump organ joins Low
years.p: Zak Sally quits after ten years. Matt Livingston takes bass and saxophone, and plays an antique pump organ that once served a Navy chaplain.

years.cap: Mimi Parker, Alan Sparhawk and bassist Matt Livingston, c. 2007
years.h: Drums and Guns is Livingston's only album
years.p: He plays bass on the record and leaves afterwards. Steve Garrington arrives the next year.

years.h: Garrington takes over bass and keys for twelve years
years.p: Steve Garrington plays on four studio albums.

eras.title: Plant takes notice, Low tests a festival crowd
eras.text: Robert Plant covered two Low songs, Sparhawk and Parker sang on a Swans album, and at Rock the Garden the band spent its whole set on one song.

years.h: Robert Plant covers Low on Band of Joy
years.p: Plant records "Monkey" and "Silver Rider," both from The Great Destroyer.
years.xp: Of Low's music, Plant said: "It's great music; it's always been in the house playing away beside Jerry Lee Lewis and Howlin' Wolf."

years.h: Low's ninth album, C'mon, has a new bassist
years.p: It's the first of four studio albums with Steve Garrington. Sub Pop makes a video for "Especially Me," and NPR records a Tiny Desk concert that year.

years.h: Sparhawk and Parker sing on Swans' "Lunacy"
years.p: They add vocals to the opening track of [[Swans|3285dc48-9505-469d-ad8a-bdf2d3dba632]]' The Seer.

years.h: Low plays one song for 27 minutes at Rock the Garden
years.p: At Minneapolis's Rock the Garden, Low stretches a slowed-down "Do You Know How to Waltz?" across its whole set. The crowd and the internet split over it.
years.xp: Sparhawk ended it with a line borrowed from an anti-drone sticker. The Invisible Way came out the same year.

years.cap: Alan Sparhawk, Mimi Parker and Steve Garrington in The Current's studio, September 2015
years.h: Ones and Sixes is Low's eleventh album
years.p: It's the third of four studio albums with Steve Garrington.

years.h: Garrington plays his last Low album, Double Negative
years.p: Sub Pop releases it and it reaches No. 26 on the UK chart. Sparhawk and Parker's voices now run through electronic distortion.

eras.title: The last album, the last show
eras.text: Parker was diagnosed with ovarian cancer late in 2020. Low made one more album, played its last show in September 2022, and ended when she died on November 5.

years.h: Parker is diagnosed with ovarian cancer
years.p: She's diagnosed in late 2020 and starts treatment in 2021. Steve Garrington has left, so Low is officially a duo for the first time.

years.h: Hey What, the last Low album, is out on Sub Pop
years.p: Liz Draper, bassist for Charlie Parr, is hired to play the songs live.

years.h: Parker tells a podcast she has cancer
years.p: In an interview on Sheroes Radio she makes her diagnosis public.
years.xp: Over 2022 Low cancels European dates in August and October and its Death Cab for Cutie support shows in September, so Parker can continue treatment.

years.h: Low plays its last show at the Water Is Life Festival
years.p: It's in Duluth, where the band started.

years.cap: Mimi Parker at Rock the Garden, Minneapolis, July 2022
years.h: Mimi Parker dies at 55
years.p: She dies of ovarian cancer on November 5, 2022, surrounded by family. Low's message the next day asks fans to keep her name close and sacred.
years.xp:
Parker was born in Duluth on September 15, 1967, and met Alan Sparhawk in grade school in Clearbrook, Minnesota. In Low she played a single snare, a cymbal and a floor tom, mostly with brushes, and sang.

She and Sparhawk had a son, Cyrus, who later played bass in Damien.

eras.title: After Low
eras.text: Sparhawk said Low was over and kept making music, first with his son in Damien, then under his own name. Plant put a Low song at the front of his 2025 album.

years.h: Damien, Sparhawk's band with his son Cyrus, releases its first album
years.p: The Boy Who Drew Cats comes out in May from a band Sparhawk formed in late 2021 with singer Marc Gartman and drummer Owen Mahon. Cyrus plays bass.

years.big: "Low is and was Mimi. It was amazing. I'm grateful."
years.h: Sparhawk tells fans the band is over
years.p: He posts it on Twitter after Parker's death, confirming Low ended with her.

years.h: Sparhawk goes solo again with White Roses, My God
years.p: It's his second solo record. In May 2025 he follows it with an album with Trampled by Turtles.

years.h: Plant leads his new album with a Low song
years.p: "Everybody's Song" is the first single from Saving Grace, fifteen years after he first covered Low.
